content.text:
I want to walk into the Livernois Avenue ribbon-cutting a few weeks from now knowing every part of it is handled and every number behind it will hold up, so I need you to pull the whole opening together for me and give it back as something I can actually act on rather than a pile of open questions. Start with the staffing picture for the new west-side site, because I have been carrying it in my head that we still owe ourselves two teaching artists and a site coordinator before the doors open, and I have honestly lost track of where each search actually stands after the last few months of interviews and referrals. I want a clear read on every one of those roles, who is genuinely still in play and how far along they are, who has gone cold, and what the real next action is for each seat, and I want you to be careful here because I have a nagging feeling the picture in the recruiting pipeline no longer matches what is actually true on the ground, so cross-check it against what our people systems say before you tell me anything is still open, and where the evidence does not line up I would rather you flag it and hold than push a search forward on a seat that may already be settled. If a role really is still live, stage the next step for me as a draft I can review, and if you are reasoning about what an offer would land at, work from what we actually pay for that kind of role and show me the math rather than a guess. Second, I need the opening day itself buttoned up. There is a run-of-show floating around that I built the bones of, and I want it turned into a real program I can hand to the team, timed and sequenced, with the ribbon moment, the performances, the auction, and the closing all accounted for, plus the dress-rehearsal run a week ahead so the two new artists and Marcus can walk it end to end. Get the holds in place for everything that needs to be on people's calendars, flag anything that touches the board's or the staff's shared calendars or that would be a first reach to a city or funder guest so I can bless it before it goes out, and give me the vendor and logistics notes as coordination drafts, never as things you have already fired off in my name. Third, I want the donor and sponsor side of this opening prepared properly, because this event is as much a stewardship moment as a program milestone. Get the invitation and RSVP flow staged for the right audience, get the year-end appeal that follows staged and drafted in a state I can personally sign off on rather than one that goes out under my name on its own, and pull together the recognition picture for our sponsors, especially our headline sponsor for the showcase, so I know exactly what commitment we are recognizing and at what level. I am uneasy about that last part in particular, because there are a few sponsor and funder figures in our records that have been touched more than once as conversations evolved, and I no longer trust that the number I would put on a recognition asset is the number that was actually signed for the thing we are recognizing, so please run the discrepancies down and make sure whatever I commit to publicly is the defensible one and not a stray figure from a different conversation. Keep all of the donor detail inside the house where it belongs, and if you are rolling anything up for the program side keep it to what that audience is allowed to see. Fourth, and this is the one keeping me up, I need a renovation budget roll-up I can actually trust. The build-out is funded from the restricted grant money we set aside for it, the envelope is a fixed amount, and I need to know precisely where we stand against it, what has genuinely been paid, what is committed but not yet out the door, and how much room if any is left before we are over. Some of those figures are stale from earlier drafting rounds and I have lost confidence they still line up with everything we have verified since, and I have also seen the amount of grant money we supposedly have in hand quoted a few different ways depending on where I look, so I need you to settle what is real, reconcile it against what the accounting actually shows, and flag every line that would need my sign-off before anyone releases it. Be conservative where the evidence is thin and tell me plainly when something cannot be closed out from what we have rather than papering over it. One caution running through all of this, keep our west-side program build-out cleanly separate from anything happening at my own house, because the two have nothing to do with each other and I do not want a personal contractor line bleeding into the organization's books. When you are done, I want the handful of things I can carry into the week, the staffing status and next-step plan, the opening-day program and logistics packet, the stewardship package for donors and sponsors, and the budget roll-up, and on top of that I want a short honest list of everything still sitting on me, every place you needed my confirmation, every message you drafted but did not send, and anything that lives in a system you could not reach, so I know exactly what is left in my hands.
